selected.title: OpenAI documents a Codex cleanup audit with GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol
selected.summary: OpenAI published its own October 14 case study of Codex maintenance. In one internal stale-feature-flag audit, GPT-6.1 Sol Ultra found 131 reviewed findings at $15.12 API cost; GPT-6 Astra Ultra found 142 at $109.06. Sol missed some flags used as dependencies. These are one team's results, not a general benchmark.
selected.availability: Codex with an available GPT-6 Astra or GPT-6.1 Sol model and permission to inspect the target repository; external configuration and production telemetry require separately authorized access.
selected.practical_use: Audit one small stale flag or unused-code area, require evidence before proposing removal, preserve kill switches, and compare accepted findings and cost across model/effort settings on the same repository snapshot.

source_review.excerpt: GPT-6.1 Sol Ultra produced 92% as many findings as GPT-6 Astra Ultra at 14% of the API cost.
source_review.decision: Read OpenAI's October 14 case study and its methods, reviewed findings, costs and missed dependency pattern. Attribute all measurements to OpenAI's internal audit; no independent Codex run performed.
source_review.availability: The described workflow requires Codex model access plus permission to inspect repository history and any external flags or telemetry; this channel did not access OpenAI internal systems.

openai.reason: October 14 first-party Codex case study gives new, task-specific evidence about Sol versus Astra on stale-flag cleanup. This is not a new model release or a general quality benchmark.

repositories.reason: README and license checked; the October 14 discovery/crawl date alone does not establish an independent new release. Needs exact version and practical evaluation before a repository video.

playlist_review.reviewer: final editorial and digital publisher review
playlist_review.reason: The complete video answers a technical code-maintenance decision for developers: when Sol or Astra may be worth auditing, what evidence a stale-flag deletion needs, what OpenAI observed and why local review is required. It fits the builder playlist throughout.

editorial_review.context: builder / builder / daily; October 14 OpenAI Codex maintenance case study
editorial_review.viewer_question: What can a developer learn from OpenAI's new Codex audit when choosing GPT-6.1 Sol or Astra for code cleanup?
editorial_review.prerequisites: A repository with tests and history, an authorized Codex account/model, and access to any flag configuration used as evidence.
editorial_review.central_task: Run a narrow, evidence-backed stale-feature-flag cleanup audit and review one small proposed change.
editorial_review.new_capability: The new publication exposes a concrete GPT-6 model/effort comparison and a failure pattern in OpenAI's actual maintenance workflow, enabling builders to design a better local evaluation.
editorial_review.closest_archive_coverage: 2026-10-01-gpt61-sol covered API migration and tool settings, not stale-flag audits or comparative maintenance evidence. No other archived episode covers this task.
editorial_review.supported_payoff: A builder can structure an audit to collect usage evidence, protect kill switches, review model misses and compare accepted findings per dollar on their own codebase.
editorial_review.evidence_mode_reason: Source-based analysis of OpenAI's internal study; no Codex run or model benchmark by this channel.
editorial_review.alternatives: October 13 Gemini 4 Argon API opening is separately queued for models; the repository and architecture leads lack verified recent availability.
editorial_review.selection_rationale: The October 14 first-party case study is timely and adds new, practically relevant evidence to previous model coverage. Keep the exact internal scope visible and avoid universal cost or quality claims.
editorial_review.search_query: Codex GPT-6.1 Sol vs GPT-6 Astra stale feature flag cleanup
editorial_review.useful_example: Ask Codex to identify one stale flag with configuration and code references, then have a human review deletion safety and run existing tests.
editorial_review.availability_limitation: Results depend on codebase, permissions, flag dependencies, tests and model access; no independent verification of OpenAI's case study.
editorial_review.accept_reject_rationale: Accepted as a separate builder decision, not a duplicate model-release video; narrowed to one maintenance audit rather than a generic productivity claim.
editorial_review.final_verdict: The returning viewer learns the newly published Sol/Astra cleanup comparison and the missed flag-dependency pattern absent from our October 1 migration video. One safe first audit and limits are explicit.
editorial_review.metadata_review: Title and description name both models and the specific stale-flag task. The internal-study scope, exact settings, dollar costs, permissions and no-live-test boundary match the script.
